scenes.heading: Tissues and specialisation
scenes.say: Almost every cell in your body carries the same DNA. So why does a neurone look and act so differently from a skin cell? It comes down to which genes each cell switches on.

scenes.heading: Same cookbook, different recipes
points: Every cell has the whole genome
Housekeeping genes: in nearly all cells
scenes.say: Think of the genome as a cookbook. Every cell carries the whole book, but each cell type only opens certain pages. Differentiation changes gene expression, not the genes themselves. Dolly the sheep proved a specialised nucleus still holds the full set.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Narrowing your options from Year 7 to a trade qualification
scenes.science: Stem cells narrow from pluripotent to fully differentiated
scenes.breaks: Cells don't choose: transcription factors, signals and cytoplasmic determinants set their fate, and they rarely change type on their own.
scenes.say: In Year 7 you could head towards almost any career, like a pluripotent stem cell. Choosing Year 11 subjects sets your path, like a cell that's determined. Once you're a qualified electrician, you're fully differentiated. Induced pluripotent stem cells are like sending an adult back to Year 7.

scenes.heading: The potency ladder
scenes.say: Climb down the potency ladder: to, plu, mul, uni. Totipotent cells make everything, including the placenta. Pluripotent cells make every body cell, but not the placenta. Multipotent cells, like blood stem cells, make several related types. Unipotent cells make just one.

scenes.heading: Every Cat Must Nap
points: Epithelial: tightly packed, covers and lines
Connective: few cells in lots of matrix
Muscle: contracts with actin and myosin
scenes.say: The four animal tissues: every cat must nap. Epithelial tissue is tightly packed and lines surfaces. Connective tissue is a few cells floating in lots of matrix, and yes, blood counts. Then muscle, and nervous tissue.

scenes.heading: Name that epithelium
scenes.question: A tube lining has one layer of tall cells with microvilli and tight junctions. What tissue is it?
scenes.say: Name an epithelium by layers plus shape. One layer means simple. Tall cells mean columnar. So it's simple columnar epithelium. Microvilli boost absorption and tight junctions control uptake, which fits the small intestine.

scenes.heading: Xylem vs phloem
scenes.say: In plants, xylem is a dead drainpipe: hollow, lignified tubes carrying water and minerals up from the roots. Phloem is a living tube with a carer: sieve tubes carry sugars both ways, kept alive by companion cells. Plants grow from meristems.

Quick recap. Cells share a genome but express different genes. Potency runs totipotent down to unipotent. There are four animal tissues. Name epithelium by layers and shape. Xylem is dead, phloem is living. Now try the practice questions!
